clue.text: One in cricket club with the unusual distinction

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter for one is placed inside the club's abbreviation

parts.note: one can be written as the indefinite article A

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the word the are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A remarkable cricketer stands out at the club for an unusual honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket club' tempts towards a sporting definition, but distinction alone defines; 'unusual' signals the rearrangement of the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is prestige or a mark of distinction that sets something apart.

clue.text: Welcoming drink

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit ... is a soft drink, diluted with water

explanation.surface: A friendly drink offered to a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial greeting is warm and friendly; a cordial is also a sweetened concentrated beverage.

clue.text: Restrict club on song

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for club in card games
a strain is a melody or snatch of music

explanation.surface: A club bans the singing of a particular tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to hold back or limit someone's freedom.

clue.text: Pole in river picked up is worn away

indicators.note: in tells us the pole goes inside the reversed river
picked up, in a down clue, means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a rod is a pole, also an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A stake planted in a river bank is gradually eaten away.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' signals reading upwards; only the river is turned, and the pole goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded describes something gradually worn down by wind, water or friction.

clue.text: We hear, sir, an international, on offer before retirement?

indicators.note: We hear tells us a word is chosen for how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
a cap is awarded to a player for each international appearance, so a player capped is an international

explanation.surface: A titled sportsman playing for his country is offered something at the end of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work; a nightcap is a drink offered before sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a last drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: The man's possibly vain

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of vain might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a particular man may well be conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a man's first name, the Russian form of John.

clue.text: Where hecklers could corner the orator

definitions.text: Where hecklers could corner the orator

parts.words: Where hecklers could corner the orator
parts.note: corner hints at Speakers' Corner, the London park spot where anyone may stand up and address passers-by, inviting heckling

explanation.surface: A place where an orator might be trapped by hostile hecklers.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner is a traditional site for public speeches in a large London royal park.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous London park contains Speakers' Corner, a site of open-air public oratory.

clue.text: Heads of church have one in readiness?

definitions.text: Heads of church have one in readiness?

indicators.note: Heads of tells us to take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Church leaders like to keep a group of singers on standby.
explanation.definitionFit: A church typically keeps a group of singers ready to lead hymns at services.

clue.text: To take place before pawn's about to surrender

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
re is Latin for 'concerning', a common crossword word for about
to cede is to give up or yield territory

explanation.surface: A chess move where a pawn is on the verge of giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or happen earlier in time or order.

clue.text: Manor's refurbished for an extortionate sum

indicators.note: refurbished means remade, so the letters of manor's are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A country house has been redone at outrageous expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a payment demanded by kidnappers, typically a huge amount.

clue.text: Fair worker's'ouse?

parts.note: hands are workers, as in farm hands; the 's gives the plural S
the apostrophe shows a dropped H, as a cockney might say house; drop the H from the synonym home too

explanation.surface: A labourer's house is described in a cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ouse signals an H dropped: home becomes 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the old sense of good-looking, as handsome is.

clue.text: Punish a supporter seen on the field

parts.note: to fine is to punish with a money penalty
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: A fan is penalised for appearing on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leg is a cricket fielding position, so a fielder stationed there is seen on the field.

clue.text: Flying object is in an indefinite form

definitions.meaning: something airborne, as a thrown ball is
undecided or uncertain, as plans may be

explanation.surface: A UFO is said to take a vague shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is aloft; plans not yet settled are likewise said to be undecided.

clue.text: Odds on press making a bloomer?

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at which a horse starts a race
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Bookmakers' odds lead the press to commit a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a blunder on the surface but here a flowering plant; spurge is a plant family.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is a flowering plant, so it literally blooms.

clue.text: Lab cope with worry that medicine is ineffective

indicators.note: with worry suggests the letters of lab cope are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Laboratory staff fret that a drug doesn't work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'medicine that is ineffective', with 'that' linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert substance given as if it were a real drug.

clue.text: Mostly get to know the versifier

indicators.note: Mostly means the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: to learn is to get to know

explanation.surface: An invitation to become acquainted with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward LEAR wrote nonsense verse and limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was a Victorian poet famous for limericks and nonsense verse.

clue.text: All bored with PE need some training. It's lamentable

indicators.note: need some training says these letters must be drilled into a new shape

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sport

explanation.surface: Pupils fed up with gym class need coaching, which is a sorry state.
explanation.definitionFit: Deplorable means deserving strong condemnation, so pitiful or regrettable.

clue.text: Spectator Syd with banter is put out

indicators.note: is put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A watching fan named Syd is annoyed by some teasing chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is an onlooker present at an event without taking part.

clue.text: Aggressive type fired up worker supporting motorway

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, puts the later pieces underneath the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
lit means set alight
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A fired-up labourer protests beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; the digit 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant is a combative activist using confrontational methods.

clue.text: Where the surfer could be a surfie?

definitions.text: Where the surfer could be a surfie?

parts.words: Where the surfer could be a surfie?
parts.note: surfie is Australian slang for a surfer, pointing to a famous Sydney surfing beach

explanation.surface: A question about where a surfer might count as a local surf enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sydney shoreline is world-famous for its waves and Australian surfing culture.

clue.text: The poet endlessly dismissed the result of overwork?

indicators.note: endlessly means the poet's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A poet is sacked without end, perhaps from working too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnout is exhaustion caused by prolonged stress and excessive work.

clue.text: The river with two islands

indicators.note: two tells us the abbreviation is written down twice

explanation.surface: A river that flows past a pair of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISIS is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the name given to the upper Thames around Oxford.

clue.text: Part of his tyre needs a basis of plastic

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man's tyre requires plastic material.
explanation.definitionFit: Styrene is the chemical monomer polymerised to make polystyrene.

clue.text: Cruel rough bit of waler for a wader

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of cruel are roughed up into a new order
bit of takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A harsh rider on a horse heads out to a shoreline bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A waler is an Australian saddle horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a long-billed shorebird that wades in mudflats.

clue.text: Go to a place to make good

definitions.meaning: to resort or betake oneself somewhere
to mend or fix something broken

explanation.surface: Someone heads off somewhere to make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to somewhere is to go there; to repair also means to fix.

clue.text: A skiing course

parts.note: a straightforward description of a prepared ski run on the slopes

explanation.surface: A ski run.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a groomed track of compacted snow for skiers.

clue.text: University bod in trouble (vigorous in style) showing reluctance to be persuaded

indicators.note: in trouble says these letters are disturbed into another order

parts.note: racy writing is lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A university student in difficulty is stubborn about changing his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is stubbornness, a refusal to change one's opinion.

clue.text: A sign, but not of times

definitions.text: A sign, but not of times

parts.words: A sign, but not of times
parts.note: a mathematical symbol for adding rather than the one for multiplication, called times

explanation.surface: A sign, but not one of the times we live in.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus sign denotes addition, unlike the multiplication cross read as times.

clue.text: Acts about in a bender, mainly back in the bar

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged acts inside the shortened, reversed joint
back tells us the shortened bender is read in reverse
mainly means the bender loses its final letter

parts.note: an elbow is a joint that bends

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of acts are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves on a drinking spree, mostly back at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims ELBOW to ELBO; 'back' reverses it to OBLE; 'about' turns ACTS into STAC, placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar in the sense of a barrier or impediment blocking progress.

clue.text: Make disparaging remarks but set for a slide?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to taunt an opposing batsman verbally
a vehicle on runners, ready to slide over snow

explanation.surface: Someone insults another player, yet is primed to slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers taunt batsmen this way; it is also a sled for sliding on snow.

clue.text: The written work to attend to is English

parts.note: to treat a patient is to attend to them

explanation.surface: Someone is told that their required reading is in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal, systematic piece of writing on a subject.

clue.text: Swing to start the game grabbing wicket

indicators.note: grabbing means the opening shot holds the wicket inside it

parts.note: to serve is to put the ball into play at the start of a tennis point
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A bowler swings the ball from the start, taking a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer or swing sharply aside.
